    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"

original_test_intent: Verify the eight temperature records represented by `TEMP_GB_RTM1~8`—presumptively PCIe retimers 1 through 8 on the GPU baseboard—are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct retimer and link-path identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the platform specification.
original_method: Confirm GB/RTM terminology, resolve eight stable BMC records, bind every RTM index to its physical retimer, PCIe route and management telemetry source, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with per-device limits under recorded system/GPU load, link state and cooling. Preserve PCIe, thermal and BMC evidence without retraining or resetting links.
manual_activity: The platform owner confirms RTM means PCIe retimer or identifies the actual component family, maps all eight devices to physical locations and PCIe routes, and supplies their thermal limits and management sources. Automation can collect eight BMC records, topology inventory and UI rows; a human resolves device/path ambiguity and owns the verdict. No link retrain, reset, traffic load or firmware action is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS and confirmation of GB/RTM terminology
Per-index retimer or other RTM physical location, part/revision/serial/firmware and board reference designator
PCIe topology mapping from each device to upstream/root/switch and downstream GPU endpoint with stable BDF identities
BMC management source for each temperature, including controller, bus, mux, device address and exact die/board field
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for every RTM1-8 sensor
Per-device units, scaling, tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, health and freshness specification
Recorded host/GPU power and load, PCIe link speed/width/state, fan mode/speeds and baseboard airflow
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser versions and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel/AER, GPU XID, PCIe or thermal logs; they are relevant to retimer and link health.
Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_GB_RTM1~8'` unless documented as one record. Enumerate and query RTM1 through RTM8 separately.
Do not map RTM index from an assumed numeric relationship to GPU index or BDF. Use the approved schematic/topology and stable device identity.
Treat I2C/I3C/management access as BMC/platform scope; host PCIe inventory alone does not prove the BMC telemetry target or temperature field.
Do not generate PCIe/GPU traffic, retrain or reset links, change link speed/power state, service the board, alter fans/thresholds or update retimer firmware. Record only the existing passive state.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped devices, stale data or BMC/UI/topology disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate RTM definition, eight-device physical/PCIe/BMC-bus topology, target, client and Script; build an eight-row expectation matrix before collection.
Retrieve RTM1-RTM8 independently with complete SDR identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.
Correlate each BMC record with its physical device and approved upstream/downstream PCIe path, while recording existing link speed/width/state, host/GPU load and cooling without changing them.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, traffic load, link retrain/reset, power/service, fan/threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Confirm RTM semantics and approve the eight-device physical, PCIe-path and BMC management-source map.
Provide per-device thermal limits, tolerance, status/freshness and exact die-versus-board field interpretation; approve the collection tool/Script.
Review RTM1 through RTM8 independently and issue the formal verdict without treating one reading, GPU temperature or link enumeration as substitute coverage.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove eight RTM records. It omits device/PCIe-path/BMC-source and UI/spec mapping, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate complete sensors, confirm all eight physical retimer-class devices, PCIe paths and BMC telemetry sources, query each record through protected read-only access, and correlate eight UI rows with the approved topology matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_GB_RTM1~8, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or manipulating PCIe links.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an eight-row matrix keyed by physical retimer-class device, stable PCIe path and BMC sensor source, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with per-device limits under recorded passive link/load/cooling state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact GPU-baseboard retimer population/topology and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/GPU-baseboard, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, retimer firmware, PCIe switch/GPU/driver inventory, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: GPU-baseboard schematic/layout and RTM index map, PCIe topology, retimer vendor thermal/telemetry definition, BMC management-bus/SDR specification, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves a range into eight physical retimer/link/source-bound records and adds passive PCIe identity evidence while preserving display-only coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Temperature display does not validate PCIe signal integrity, error rate, bandwidth, equalization, failover, link retraining, retimer firmware or alarm/protection behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: RTM semantics, eight-device physical/PCIe/BMC map, per-device acceptance, passive-state timing, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RTM numbering can differ between schematic, SMBus and PCIe paths; telemetry may be retimer die or nearby board temperature; link topology can change with platform population.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or retimer-vendor telemetry as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/field and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate RTM1-8 device identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. PCIe link status alone is not equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS, confirmed RTM terminology and eight-row physical device, part/firmware/reference-designator and PCIe-path matrix
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source for every RTM1-8 record
Complete separate raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps plus separate redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Recorded PCIe topology and existing link speed/width/state, host/GPU load, fan/baseboard airflow and per-device Project/vendor tolerance with no link manipulation

Explicit missing/duplicate/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-traffic/no-retrain-or-reset/no-service/no-retry proof, final PCIe/GPU/BMC health and engineer-owned eight-device verdict

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, arbitrary GPU mapping or generic module temperature from being presented as eight retimer readings, and prevents PCIe load, retraining or reset from being added to a passive display test.
independent_technical_reasoning: Eight RTM channels on a GPU baseboard most plausibly represent PCIe retimers, but the acronym and numbering are platform-owned facts. Each reading must therefore bind to a physical retimer, its PCIe route and the BMC telemetry field. A readable temperature says nothing about PCIe signal integrity, so link testing or retraining would be unauthorized coverage expansion.
